If he had no knowledge of their situation, the decision might be different, but knowing makes it more about whether he's being compassionate or not. I also recall the term "merciless" mentioned in the scenario. Being merciless means lacking compassion or pity. James's action fits this description because he's not showing any mercy to his tenants in their time of need. So, putting it all together, James's decision to increase the rent despite knowing his tenants' financial struggles seems morally wrong because it lacks compassion and makes their situation harder. It's an example of being merciless in a situation where mercy would be more appropriate.
